A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GENA3D and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Existing content can be matched reliably despite pagination changes and added supplementary sections.

before.justification: v2 reports original GSO benchmark comparisons, component and input-view ablations, occlusion-level experiments, and qualitative real-world results (Tables 1–5 and B.1).

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds controlled comparisons, robustness and fusion experiments, human preferences, and failure examples (Sections B.5–B.6 and Appendix C).

M1.justification: Sections 3 and A.1 retain the same view-wise attention, visibility-weighted fusion, stereo-conditioned attention, gating, and training objective. The new fusion alternatives are ablations, not replacements for the proposed method.

E1.justification: The datasets and amodal 3D generation task remain unchanged. Section B.5 adds deliberately corrupted 2D-completion and MVS inputs, while Appendix C adds explicit failure scenarios, extending input-condition coverage within the existing domains.

E2.justification: Existing baseline comparisons are retained. Table B.2 newly evaluates Amodal3R equipped with OAAC against GENA3D, adding a comparator with the same 2D completion front-end.

E3.justification: Existing training and benchmark settings are retained, but new studies substantially expand the evaluation design: a 100-object ablation sample, 5%/10% Gaussian perturbations, a 100-GSO-object × 10-viewpoint pose check, and human comparisons using 30 objects and 10 raters at 1, 2, and 4 input views (Sections B.5–B.6).

E4.justification: Beyond v2's existing ablations and qualitative MVS-error examples, v3 adds matched-front-end controls, quantitative upstream-error propagation, alternative fusion strategies, empirical pose-consistency checks, human corroboration of PCS rankings, and illustrated failure analysis (Tables B.2–B.5 and Figure C.1). These address several previously untested questions.

E5.justification: Section B.6 introduces inter-rater reliability reporting, giving 77.8% pairwise agreement for the human study. Neither version reports repeated model-run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and B.1 retain their values. New Table B.2 reports FID 32.04 for GENA3D versus 36.85 for Amodal3R+OAAC on the new 100-object evaluation. Table B.5 adds GENA3D preference rates of 65.4%, 74.1%, and 78.2% for 1/2/4 views. Perturbation, fusion, 97.6% canonical-output, and failure findings are also new; these are additional results, not improvements over v2 under identical settings.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the mathematical method definitions are unchanged. The new pose-invariance check is empirical; no theorem, proof, formal assumption, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about bridging 2D priors and 3D coherence through the two attention mechanisms. The supplementary evidence supports those claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: v2 already discusses MVS self-correction and possible mismatch with ground-truth geometry. v3 adds specific limits involving unidentifiable objects or poses, often under extreme (>85%) occlusion, and catastrophic 2D-completion failures (Appendix C). It also interprets the new controls and human preferences as support for the architecture and perceptual advantage.

D1.justification: Section B.5 adds procedural details for the new tests: noise applied to completed image regions, point-cloud depth noise scaled by maximum bounding-box extent, and pose consistency measured through pairwise rotation alignment. Existing architecture, training, hardware, and project-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 86 references are retained. Additional Amodal3R experiments extend the evidence without substantively revising the paper's novelty or relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: Existing prose is essentially unchanged. v3 adds Sections B.5, B.6, and C with explanations of the new analyses and makes a small project-link presentation edit; there is no extensive rewriting or narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables B.2–B.5 and the failure montage in Figure C.1, repositions Figure B.1 within the appendix, and tightens table and figure spacing so the conclusion fits on page 14. Existing displays are retained; the visual changes are localized additions and layout refinements.

improvement.justification: The matched-OAAC comparison, human preferences, and controlled robustness tests provide useful additional support for v2's conclusions, while Appendix C makes failure boundaries clearer. These are targeted improvements in evidential support and qualification. Their strength remains limited by the small supplementary samples, brief protocol descriptions, and absence of uncertainty estimates; agreement in preference rankings also does not fully validate PCS as a metric.
